Subject: CareCurve deployment trade-offs: HIPAA/BAA evidence & path recommendation

Hi Elaine — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned before you loop in procurement/security: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary constraint: CareCurve needs to support PHI in production and must complete an external HIPAA audit within Q4.
- Preference leaning toward private or heavily isolated deployments, but open to options if we can provide controls/evidence quickly.
- Key questions: encryption key ownership, SOC2 evidence, timeline for BAA negotiation, expected daily PHI volume and latency SLOs.

Deployment options and trade-offs (short):
1) Hosted API (Redwood managed)
   - Pros: fastest to production, minimal infra overhead, standard BAA template, can provide current SOC2 report and SOC2 summary (attached).
   - Cons: data flows through Redwood environment; we offer customer-scoped access controls and encryption, but key management is with Redwood unless you request a Bring-Your-Own-Key option (BYOK) — BYOK is supported in Dedicated/Private flows first.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool)
   - Pros: single-tenant GPU pool, logical data isolation, predictable throughput and pricing. We can scope SOC2 evidence to include this environment and offer BYOK via KMS integration.
   - Cons: slightly longer lead time (2-4 weeks) and a commitment for reserved capacity is typical for pricing advantages.
3) Private VPC / On-prem appliance
   - Pros: customer-managed network, data never leaves your VPC or on-prem cluster; best fit for strict audit controls and regulatory reviews. We can provide an on-prem bundle and runbook.
   - Cons: procurement and install timeline (4-8+ weeks depending on on-prem), additional integration work for telemetry/audit exports.

Immediate asks from our side to size the right recommendation:
- Estimated monthly tokens / daily PHI transactions (ballpark)
- Any current KMS/HSM provider or key ownership requirements
- Do you need continuous audit logs exported to your SIEM? If so which vendor?
- Who on your procurement/security team should we include (email) for the BAA and vendor questionnaire?

Attachments: BAA draft (initial), SOC2 summary (redacted).

Proposed next step: I can send the BAA draft and SOC2 summary now (attached) and Markus can follow up with a short tech note comparing encryption/BYOK behaviors across the three options and a ballpark cost delta. If that looks good, we can schedule a 30-min call with your security lead and procurement this Thursday or Friday.

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu

- SOC2: are the SOC2 artifacts for Hosted the same as for Dedicated? Will you provide a scoped SOC2 report that references our tenancy/isolation?

Hi Elaine — quick technical follow-up and proposed options based on your constraints. Thanks for the volume and SLO details — that helps.

Short answers
- BYOK: Hosted API offers BYOK via our managed KMS gateway only for certain enterprise agreements; for guaranteed customer key ownership we recommend Dedicated or Private (both support direct KMS integrations and HSM workflows). We can provision a Dedicated instance with your KMS (AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault) within the Dedicated flow.
- SOC2 scope: Our SOC2 report covers Redwood's control environment; for Dedicated we can provide a SOC2 SOC-coverage letter that explains the isolation model and how controls apply to a dedicated pool. For Private, since the environment is customer-managed, we provide guidance and documentation for your auditor plus our vendor controls evidence.
- Audit logs: Dedicated and Private support real-time export of request and response metadata to your SIEM (Kafka/Splunk endpoints or S3 export). Hosted can provide near-real-time logs to a customer-managed S3 bucket and redacted request traces; we can surface immutable append-only logs in the Dedicated offering.
- Timeline: If you decide on Dedicated this week, contract + infra provisioning typically completes in ~2-3 weeks; that should meet a mid-November audit window if procurement moves quickly. Private/on-prem will likely miss that window because of install scheduling.

Ballpark cost deltas (very high level)
- Hosted API: lowest ramp cost, consumption pricing; typical monthly starting range for your volume: $6k-$12k (depends on model/throughput patterns).
- Dedicated: baseline reserved capacity + usage delta; estimated starting commit for target SLO/volume: $18k-$30k/month depending on instance size and burst allowances.
- Private/on-prem: one-time setup + ongoing support; estimate depends on hardware; we can produce an SOW if you want a firm number.

Attached: BAA draft and SOC2 summary (redacted). I've also added a short tech note in the Drive link that maps which evidence we can provide immediately vs what requires extra scoping for audit.

Next steps I suggest
1) Jasmine will coordinate a 30-min meeting with your procurement/security this week;
2) We finalize a Dedicated sizing worksheet if you want to pursue that path;
3) We circulate the BAA and an initial SOW/quote to procurement.

If you prefer, I can join the call to run through encryption and log export specifics.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Infra & Security Solutions, Redwood Inference
